facts.material: bi-metal (HSS teeth on steel) hole saws, steel mandrels and pilot drills, plastic carry case
facts.function: cutting circular holes in wood, drywall, plastic and metal with a power drill
facts.form: retail kit of several hole saws, mandrels with pilot drills, fitted carrying case
facts.end_use: hand-held power drill use by trades and DIY consumers

gri_path: GRI 1 fails: components are prima facie in different headings (hole saws 8202, mandrels 8466.10 per H278181, pilot drills 8207.50, case 4202)
GRI 3(b) retail set: different articles, put up together for the single activity of cutting holes, packed for retail sale without repacking
Essential character from the hole saws, which do the cutting and dominate the set's role in use (HQ H097658, NY N355088)
GRI 5(a): the fitted carrying case is classified with the set

rejected_alternatives.reason: tool holders; mandrels alone are classified there (H278181), but they do not give the kit its essential character
interchangeable drilling tools; the pilot drills only guide the saw and are secondary
the case is a fitted container classified with the set under GRI 5(a)

classification.rationale: The kit is a GRI 3(b) retail set of hole saws, mandrels with pilot drills and a fitted case, put up together to cut holes. HQ H097658 classified an essentially identical bi-metal hole saw kit in 8202.99.00 because the hole saws give essential character; H278181 later modified it only as to the separate classification of mandrels (8466.10.01), not the kit. NY N355088 (2025, in force) confirms hole saw sets in 8202.99.0000.
